title: Ambani vs Adani
summary: Compare how Mukesh Ambani's Reliance and Gautam Adani's businesses earn money, expand and face risk, without confusing people, companies or cash.
objectives: Distinguish the leaders, RIL consolidated, AEL consolidated and separately reported Adani businesses.
Explain how fuel/chemicals, Jio, retail, ports and power earn money.
Separate sales, accounting earnings and operating/investing/financing cash flows.
Trace how integration and upfront investment can grow a business without guaranteeing immediate profit.
Compare risks using the right company, period, units and measure.

steps.title: Names are not money boxes

state.caption: Begin with labelled lunchboxes
state.note:
Role tags are not accounts.
Lunchbox sizes do not measure wealth.

steps.narration: Picture labelled lunchboxes for company accounts. First, set the name tags aside: Mukesh Ambani leads Reliance Industries Limited, or **RIL**; Gautam Adani chairs the Adani Group. [S1] [S3] These role labels identify people, not the money inside a company's lunchbox. This lesson compares businesses, not personal fortunes.
whatChanged: + two leader-role tags
~ no company totals yet

steps.title: One reporting lunchbox

state.caption: Choose the reporting outline
state.note:
Selected compartments, not every business.
One outline for controlled businesses.

steps.narration: Now put selected Reliance businesses into compartments: energy and materials, digital services and retail. [S1] One reporting outline brings the parent and businesses it controls into a combined account. [S2] Think of the outline as the lunchbox lid; it tells you which compartments belong in the total.
whatChanged: + RIL outline and compartments

steps.title: A group of separate lunchboxes

state.caption: A banner is not a single lunchbox
state.note:
Separate company lunchboxes.
The dotted banner is portfolio context.

steps.narration: The Adani banner sits above separate lunchboxes. **AEL** means Adani Enterprises; **APSEZ** means Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone; **AGEL** means Adani Green Energy. AEL develops businesses, but separately reported companies also appear in the wider portfolio. [S3] [S10] A shared banner does not turn their accounts into AEL's account.
whatChanged: + distinct AEL, APSEZ and AGEL boxes

steps.title: The outline changes the answer

state.caption: Read the boundary before the number
state.note:
RIL consolidated ≠ AEL + every Adani firm.
Real ownership is more complex than lunchboxes.

steps.narration: Choose the lunchbox before reading its total. Combining a parent and controlled subsidiaries into one economic entity is **consolidation**. [S2] RIL consolidated and AEL consolidated each have their own outline; AEL is not all Adani businesses. [S3] [S10] The lunchbox analogy leaves out the finer details of ownership.

callout.text: Shared leadership or branding alone does not make one consolidated company. IFRS 10 explains the concept; this is not a claim that these issuers directly report under IFRS. [S2]

whatChanged: ~ RIL outline and AEL-only box highlighted

steps.title: Start with a paying customer

state.caption: Follow a product, service and payment
state.note:
Empty lanes: add earning engines next.
Payment arrows show direction, not amounts.

steps.narration: Begin with a customer paying for a product or service: fuel, shopping, connectivity or cargo handling. [S5] [S8] Customer receipts belong to operating activity; cash spent on assets or raised through borrowing answers different questions. [S4] We'll add each earning engine without merging the company accounts.
whatChanged: + delivery and customer-payment arrows

steps.title: Reliance: fuel and chemicals

state.caption: Product prices must cover costs
state.costs:
Sales less feedstock and operating costs:
inspect the margin, not crude alone.

steps.narration: Reliance's **Oil-to-Chemicals**, or O2C, sells fuels and chemicals. Feedstock is the raw material used to make them. Selling prices must cover feedstock and operating costs; the gap matters for earnings. RIL identifies fuel-margin conditions and feedstock sourcing as drivers, so rising crude prices alone do not tell you the profit story. [S5]
whatChanged: + fuel/chemicals engine and feedstock input

steps.title: Reliance: connections and shopping

state.caption: Different customers, different engines
state.note:
Subscriptions and retail sales differ.
More customers alone do not establish profit.

steps.narration: Jio's connectivity engine earns through subscriptions and digital services; subscriber additions and spending per user support revenue. [S6] Retail earns by selling goods through stores and digital platforms, including electronics, fashion and groceries. [S7] These are different businesses inside the RIL reporting outline, not one identical margin machine.
whatChanged: + connectivity and shopping engines

steps.title: Adani: moving cargo
steps.narration: APSEZ receives income from ports and linked cargo services. Its shore-to-door model connects port handling, rail, logistics parks, warehousing and road delivery. [S8] Linking the journey helps explain what customers pay for. Cargo handled is a physical volume; it is not the same thing as revenue or profit.
whatChanged: + APSEZ port, rail and warehouse service chain

steps.title: Adani: power and airports

state.caption: Keep the power and airport boxes distinct
state.note:
Electricity sales ≠ generating capacity.
Airport activity sits in AEL's reporting box.

steps.narration: AGEL develops and operates renewable-energy assets and earns power-supply revenue from electricity sales. Capacity measures what assets can generate, not money received. [S9] Airports are an AEL incubating business, with airport activity contributing income in that reporting box. [S3] Neither belongs inside APSEZ's ports results.

callout.text: Ports and renewables are examples, not all Adani businesses; the wider portfolio includes other utilities and cement. [S10]

whatChanged: + AGEL power and AEL airport engines

steps.title: Link services, not legal accounts

state.caption: Integration coordinates services
state.note: Service links do not redraw company boundaries.

steps.narration: **Integration** means connecting useful activities. APSEZ links cargo services across the delivery journey. [S8] Reliance stores distribute Jio services and devices and support JioMart local fulfilment. [S7] These connections can support customer access, but a service link alone does not establish control or merge legal accounts. [S2]

callout.text: Avoid a tidy industrial-versus-consumer split: Reliance also has industrial infrastructure, while Adani also has consumer-facing airports. [S5] [S3]

whatChanged: ~ service links highlighted
~ entity boundaries retained

steps.title: Build first, earn later

state.caption: Illustrative cash timing · not company data

steps.narration: **Capital expenditure**, or capex, builds or buys long-lived assets before their full earnings arrive. Operating cash, new owner investment called equity, and loans can fund construction. [S4] Reliance reports capex and financing facilities; Adani reports portfolio capex and AEL's rights issue, an equity fundraising. [S5] [S10] The tank is illustrative, not company cash data.

callout.text: EBITDA, an accounting earnings measure, and management-defined cash profit are not verified operating cash flow. Check the cash-flow reconciliation before treating earnings as construction funding. [S4] [S5] [S10]

whatChanged: + three funding routes and construction clock

steps.title: Growth can still pressure profit

state.caption: Illustrative ramp · completion is not profit

steps.narration: An opened asset can take time to earn fully. **Depreciation** spreads an asset's cost through accounting earnings; interest and repayment timing also matter. [S3] [S4] AEL identifies new-asset depreciation affecting profit. [S3] Competition and weaker customer demand can interrupt the ramp in other engines too. [S6] [S7]

callout.text: Bigger capacity or revenue is not a universal winner. Inspect earnings, cash and investment timing at the right boundary. This lesson is not an investment recommendation. [S3] [S4]

whatChanged: ~ construction asset becomes operational
~ funding tokens move into the tank
+ earnings-ramp and obligation markers

steps.title: Sales, earnings and cash differ

state.caption: Three accounting labels, separate cash

cards.title: PAT
cards.text:
Profit after tax
Accounting bottom line

state.note:
Issuer EBITDA adjustments can differ.
Earnings are not the bank balance.

steps.narration: **Revenue** is the sales/top-line measure. **EBITDA** means earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation; issuer adjustments can differ. **PAT** is profit after tax. [S5] [S10] These accounting measures are not cash flows: non-cash items and payment timing require reconciliation. [S4]
whatChanged: + accounting cards and a distinct cash-flow card

steps.title: Three cash-flow questions

state.caption: Classify the cash movement

flows.title: Financing
flows.text:
Equity and borrowing
Repayments also matter

state.note:
A new loan is financing cash,
not customer revenue.

steps.narration: **Operating** cash flows cover the main revenue-producing activities, such as customer receipts and day-to-day payments. **Investing** covers acquiring or disposing of long-term assets. **Financing** changes equity and borrowings, including loan receipts and repayments. [S4] A bank loan adds financing cash; it does not create customer sales or accounting profit.
whatChanged: ~ cash split into operating, investing and financing routes

steps.title: Match period, units and boundary

state.caption: Evidence cards · not a size ranking
state.note:
1 crore = 10 million rupees.
Annual flows, not balances at a date.

steps.narration: Use FY2025–26, ending 31 March 2026, and rupees in **crore**; one crore means ten million. RIL reports revenue ₹11,75,919 crore, AEL total income ₹1,02,943 crore, and APSEZ revenue ₹38,736 crore. [S5] [S3] [S8] AGEL activity measures and portfolio aggregates also retain their own boundaries. [S9] [S10] These are annual flows, not current trading data.

callout.text: Same currency does not make AEL total income equivalent to RIL revenue. Align company, period, units and measure before comparing; do not add portfolio totals to component companies. [S3] [S5] [S10]

whatChanged: ~ period, units, entity and source labels preserved

steps.title: Debt belongs to the borrower

state.caption: Different scopes, no winner meter
state.maturity:
APSEZ average debt maturity: 5.4 years.
Cash and debt snapshot: 31 March 2026.
state.note:
Check the borrower, available cash
and when repayment falls due.

steps.narration: **Net debt/EBITDA** compares debt after cash offsets with an annual earnings measure; it is not a cash-flow ratio. APSEZ reports 1.9× and average debt maturity of 5.4 years at 31 March 2026. [S8] The Adani portfolio separately reports 3.3×. [S10] Ask which borrower owes money, can access cash and must repay when.

callout.text: Portfolio cash is not established here as freely transferable to every company. APSEZ's ratio cannot represent every Adani borrower. [S8] [S10]

whatChanged: ~ entity ratio kept separate from portfolio context

steps.title: Ask what could interrupt earnings

state.caption: Match the risk to the earning engine
state.note:
Risk questions guide inspection;
they are not forecasts of failure.

steps.narration: Test the engine, not the surname. O2C depends on product/feedstock margins. [S5] Jio faces price competition and technology risks; Retail faces spending and sourcing risks. [S6] [S7] APSEZ discusses tariff uncertainty and geopolitical disruption. [S8] AEL highlights depreciation after new assets open. [S3] Growing activity does not guarantee growing profit.

quiz.q: You want the whole Adani portfolio. Is AEL's consolidated statement enough?
options: Yes, because AEL is the flagship
No, separately reported businesses also matter
Yes, because the chairman is shared
No, only personal wealth can measure it
quiz.why: AEL is not every Adani company. Its consolidated boundary differs from the wider portfolio, which includes separately reported businesses. [S3] [S10]

quiz.q: A company gets a new bank loan. What changed?
options: Its customer sales rose
Its operating profit rose
Its product margins rose
Its financing cash inflow rose
quiz.why: Borrowing adds financing cash. It does not create customer revenue or accounting profit. [S4]

quiz.q: Crude costs rise but selling prices do not. What should you inspect?
options: Product margins and feedstock costs
Only the chairman's personal wealth
Only the number of Jio customers
Whether all loans became revenue
quiz.why: O2C economics depend on product/feedstock margins. Inspect the gap between selling prices and input costs rather than assuming crude's direction tells the earnings story. [S5]

quiz.q: Connecting a port, rail and warehouse helps explain what?
options: Why every group company is merged
Why cargo demand can never fall
How linked cargo services earn income
How borrowing becomes customer sales
quiz.why: APSEZ's shore-to-door model links cargo services customers pay for. A service connection is not a merger of every group company's accounts. [S8] [S2]

quiz.q: A profitable business builds an airport. Why might it need finance?
options: Profit makes asset construction free
Construction needs cash before earnings ramp
Every completed asset avoids depreciation
Borrowing removes future repayment costs
quiz.why: Upfront asset investment and accounting profit have different cash timing. New assets may contribute earnings gradually, while construction already needs funding. [S4] [S3] [S10]

quiz.q: Can APSEZ's debt ratio represent every Adani business?
options: Yes, shared names make debt identical
Yes, ports finance all group activity
Yes, all companies have equal earnings
No, assess debt at the entity boundary
quiz.why: APSEZ's ratio describes APSEZ. The separately reported portfolio ratio has a wider scope; neither establishes identical debt risk for every company. [S8] [S10]

quiz.q: Two rupee figures have unlike boundaries and labels. What first?
options: Align company, period, units and measure
Pick the larger figure as the winner
Add the portfolio to its component firms
Treat total income as operating cash
quiz.why: Currency alone does not align reporting measures or company boundaries. Keep source labels such as total income, revenue and activity-specific measures intact. [S3] [S5] [S9] [S10]

quiz.q: Does a count-specific dismissal prove every allegation false?
options: Yes, all companies share one court result
Yes, any dismissal is a merits verdict
No, read the order's exact scope
No, earlier allegations prove guilt
quiz.why: The order specifies counts and defendants and disclaims an opinion on the merits. Neither allegations nor this dismissal establish a verdict about every business or allegation. [S11] [S12]
